analysis.investment_thesis: IXIGO rides a genuine India travel digitization wave — trains and buses are massively underpenetrated for OTA booking — but at 133x trailing P/E with net profit *declining* from ₹73Cr to ₹60Cr in FY25, the price demands perfection the business has not yet earned. I love the sector; I cannot love the stock at this price.
key_strengths: Revenue grew 68.5% CAGR (₹40Cr → ₹914Cr FY19-25) with FY25 OCF of ₹122Cr — finally generating real cash
Asset-light OTA model with 81.74% gross margin and near-zero debt (D/E 0.04) — clean balance sheet
Multi-brand dominance in trains/buses (ixigo + ConfirmTkt + AbhiBus) — structural moat in a segment IRCTC cannot fully serve
key_risks: Valuation is absurd — 133x P/E, 119x EV/EBITDA, for a business earning 7% operating margins with declining net profit
Net profit fell ₹73Cr → ₹60Cr in FY25 despite revenue growing 39% — quality of earnings is poor, heavily reliant on ₹39Cr other income in FY24
No promoter holding disclosed; 64% FII concentration means any global risk-off triggers sharp selling with no domestic anchor
red_flags: Net profit declined YoY (₹73Cr → ₹60Cr) while revenue grew 39% — operating leverage is absent at 7% margins
Other income of ₹23-39Cr materially inflates reported profits; core EBIT-level profitability is fragile
ROE of only 9.74% — well below my 15% minimum — on a company priced for exceptional compounding
analysis.detailed_analysis:
IXIGO is a legitimate India consumption story — digital travel booking, especially for trains and buses, has a decade of penetration growth ahead of it. Revenue compounding at 68.5% CAGR and FCF of ₹118Cr in FY25 shows the business model works. The multi-brand strategy across ixigo, ConfirmTkt, and AbhiBus creates genuine reach in Tier 2/3 India where travel demand is exploding. I respect the execution so far.

But I am a buyer of businesses, not stories. At 133x trailing P/E and 119x EV/EBITDA with a 7% operating margin and a net profit that shrank last year, the market has priced in perfection for the next 10 years today. I have seen too many good businesses destroyed by bad entry prices. When margins expand, FCF compounds, and the P/E comes below 40x on real earnings power — not other income — I will revisit this with great interest. Until then, I will watch from the sidelines.
